title: How the Vision Termination Credit Is Computed — Premium Billing Accounts Premium Accounting
content:
**Clause.** On Premium Billing Accounts, the termination credit for a vision plan unit is the amount per month multiplied by the months counted, rounded half up to the cent once, on the final figure. The amount per month is the unit's filed monthly premium; the months counted are the months billed after the unit's termination month that have begun.

**The unit.** The vision plan unit is the plan unit of the subscriber's Vision Plans enrollment funded by the account that shows a voluntary termination — that is, every vision enrollment of the subscriber funded by the account, the subscriber's own and each enrollee's, which share that enrollment's plan, coverage tier and dates and are read from it. Where more than one such subscriber enrollment is on record, the unit is read from the one with the latest termination date, and of two with the same termination date the one recorded first. Where the account funds no subscriber vision enrollment ended by voluntary termination, the termination credit is 0.00.

**The filed monthly premium.** The monthly premium of the unit's Vision Plans plan for the unit's coverage tier, as that plan's premium schedule states it.

**Months billed after the termination month.** The whole calendar months from the month after the month of the unit's termination date through the latest coverage month billed on the account, the latest coverage month billed being the coverage month of the invoice issued last (of two issued on the same day, the one recorded first). They are zero when the account carries no invoice, or when that coverage month is not later than the termination month.

**Months that have begun.** The whole calendar months from the unit's termination date to the credit date, plus one — whole months counted the way an anniversary is counted, a month being complete only when a later month reaches the same day number, the last day of a shorter month not completing it — never fewer than zero and never more than the months billed after the termination month. A billed month not yet begun is credited once it begins.

**Posting.** The credit is posted against the coverage month of the invoice issued last.

**Worked example (hypothetical figures).**
| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Filed monthly premium | 13.25 |
| Termination date | 31 March |
| Coverage month of the invoice issued last | July of the same year |
| Credit date | 10 May |

Months billed after the termination month: April through July, 4. Whole months from 31 March to 10 May: 30 April does not complete a month (a shorter month's last day), so 1 complete month; plus one gives 2 months that have begun, which is not more than 4. Credit: 13.25 multiplied by 2, 26.50, posted against July. Had the credit date been 31 July, the months that have begun would be 4 complete months plus one, 5, held to the 4 months billed: 53.00.
